text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Tuesday it would change its legal structure over the next 12 months and improve the efficiency of a "poison pill" protecting the company against hostile takeovers.
Spokesman Corneel Maes of Fortis AG, the Belgian arm, said the changes, approved at a Fortis AG extraordinary shareholders meeting on Monday, were aimed at improving the cohesion within the group.
"This is internal reshuffling, (but) it will simplify the structure. It was quite complex like this," Maes said.
When Fortis was formed in 1990, Fortis AG and Fortis AMEV each took a 50 percent stake in two operational holdings -- Belgian AG 1824 and Dutch AMEV-VSB 1990.
"But since then the group has developed, there have been quite a few acquisitions," Maes said.
Under the original structure, each of the parent companies had the right to exercise an option to buy the other parent's 50-percent stake in its operational holding in the event of a takeover bid.
"The purpose was to scare off raiders," Maes said.
"But now the poison pill is being extended, it now applies to the whole group," he said.
When Fortis was formed, only AG 1824 and AMEV-VSB 1990 had been named (for the option right), Maes added.
Under the new structure, Fortis will have four operational holdings -- Fortis Belgium, Fortis Netherlands , Fortis International and Fortis U.S. Inc.
For Fortis Belgium and Fortis Netherlands, the legal structure is not yet up and running, Maes said.
The new structure will also enable the group to integrate Belgian bank ASLK/CGER entirely into Fortis Belgium. ASLK is now incorporated in Amev-VSB 1990.
